lessons.title: 2. Interfaces & Union Narrowing
lessons.description: Interfaces describe object shapes, and TypeScript treats a comparison like typeof input === 'number' as a type guard that narrows a union. Keep the exported User interface and implement getId(input: number | User): number: return input directly for numbers, or input.id for User objects. The test checks both union cases.

tests.name: test_get_id
tests.unittest_code:
if (solution.getId(10) !== 10) throw new Error('number case failed');
if (solution.getId({ id: 20, name: 'Bob' }) !== 20) throw new Error('User case failed');

learning_objectives: Narrow union types with typeof type guards
Write functions over number | object unions

source.name: TypeScript Handbook — Narrowing — typeof type guards

exercises.question: Implement the exported `describe(input: number | string): string` so it returns 'number' for a number and 'string' for a string, using a `typeof` check to narrow the union.

tests.name: test_describe_number
tests.test_code: if (solution.describe(7) !== 'number') throw new Error('number case failed');

tests.name: test_describe_string
tests.test_code: if (solution.describe('seven') !== 'string') throw new Error('string case failed');

tests.name: test_describe_zero
tests.test_code: if (solution.describe(0) !== 'number') throw new Error('zero case failed');
